turnaround_reason: Stock down ~58% from 52wk high on debt-load concerns (D/E 178%, $5.9B debt) and an S&P downgrade to 'BB' in March 2026, compounded by a Q1 2026 swing to a $43M net loss and an EBITDA guide cut of ~20% for the year. A new CEO (started Jan 2026) is resetting the base with cost discipline and lower capex.
bullish_points: Heavy, broad insider buying over the last 6 months: directors purchased at $9.84-$11.36, well above the current $10.04 price, net +301k shares bought vs sold
Cheap on forward multiples: fwd P/E 8.6x, EV/EBITDA 7.0x, P/B 0.91x
Company reaffirmed full-year adjusted cash flow guidance of $700-800M despite the downgrade
Reduced inventory $48M in Q1, showing early balance-sheet discipline under new CEO
Net sales still grew +2% in Q1 despite the earnings miss
bearish_points: S&P downgraded issuer rating to 'BB' from 'BB+' in March 2026 citing debt burden and market weakness
2026 EBITDA guidance was cut ~20% - the deleveraging story is not yet confirmed
Q1 2026 swung to a $43M net loss vs $127M net income in Q1 2025
FCF improvement is coming mostly from lower capex, not operational improvement - lower quality
Very thin margins (net margin 3.2%, operating margin 4.1%) leave little room for error on a highly levered balance sheet
catalyst: Q2 2026 earnings (Aug 4) - watch for EBITDA trajectory vs the cut guidance and any further debt/rating commentary from the new CEO
suggested_trade: Spot position, small size - the insider buying and cheap multiple are real signals but the debt/EBITDA trajectory is still unconfirmed
key_risk: EBITDA continues to deteriorate faster than guided, forcing another rating downgrade and squeezing an already-levered balance sheet
would_skip_if: Q2 earnings show EBITDA guidance cut again or free cash flow guidance is walked back
